design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing in six words of plain English: put the automation plan at Northgate back on. Nothing she says names a support overage, arrears, a late fee or a point true-up, and none of the three numbers the task scores can be looked up anywhere. To reach them the agent has to read the published rules, see from the plan's own history that the plan year's 16.0 included support hours are overdrawn by 30.5 hours with nothing invoiced for them, work out from the ledger what the uncovered work costs, discover from the reinstatement rule that the charge waits on the balance owed standing at nil or below, work out what it takes to get it there, hand the payment to the caller, and only then put the plan back into service. The difficulty is in discovering which problems must be solved and in getting three multi-factor figures exactly right over a real ledger and two other product lines, not in choosing among similar tools.

SCOPE: ALREADY CLAIMED, THIS TASK, STILL TO COME. This is the first task of the difficulty, so nothing was occupied before it. It claims controls_ext_support_overage_charge (support hours beyond the pool, on controls_invoice_charged), controls_ext_arrears_settlement (the owner's own payment, on controls_payment_received) and controls_ext_reinstatement_charge (restoring monitoring, on controls_plan_reinstated), together with their three tools charge_controls_support_overage_c0d5009e, record_controls_plan_payment_09134fd7 and reinstate_controls_plan_58d0efe4. Left untouched for task 1, whose draw is one prerequisite problem: the alarm side of the charter (controls_credit_issued and the monitoring rules) and the software side (controls_software_update_applied and the upgrade labor rules), with the customer's own act there being the authorisation of upgrade labor rather than a payment. The two tasks share no policy, no tool and no write parameter.

STEP 0 DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0002_commercial_hvac_service_contractor/tasks/controls_support_desk --tasks 2):
{"task": 0, "key": "commercial_hvac_service_contractor/controls_support_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 6]}
{"task": 1, "key": "commercial_hvac_service_contractor/controls_support_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 6]}
The tree therefore has exactly two prerequisite problems besides the root, and each of the three computations declares exactly six factors. The support overage took 6, the settlement 6 and the reinstatement 6, matching the drawn multiset [6, 6, 6].

THE LONG AND BROAD DEPENDENCY. Surface goal (put the plan back on) -> the reinstatement rule states that the charge is raised only once the balance owed under the plan stands at nil or below, and the records show 3130.00 owed -> the settlement rule states that the sum required is fixed only after every hour of uncovered controls support work stands invoiced on the plan's billing history, and the records show no such charge -> the support overage rule turns 46.5 logged hours and 16.0 credited hours into 2462.32. That is the depth: two hops, neither of which the caller mentions and neither of which can be swapped. The breadth sits at each hop: the overage reads the ticket ledger by closure method and by channel, the tier's rates and allowances, and the building's maintenance agreement (three separate factors turn on it); the settlement reads the whole charge and payment ledger, the due-day clock, the tier's instalment and licence true-up frequency, the covered point count against the tier's maximum, the owner's energy subscription and the maintenance tier's repair labor cover; the reinstatement reads the withdrawal day, the covered points and panels, the invoice count, the graphics-edit count, the software update history, the maintenance agreement and the energy subscription.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
Root problem: controls_ext_reinstatement_charge (the caller's request points at it).
Edge A: controls_ext_arrears_settlement waits on controls_ext_support_overage_charge. kind value_input; gate outstanding_charges, a real compute binding of the settlement; form state. Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from the settlement's own rule: "The sum required to settle a plan is fixed only after every hour of controls support work the plan's included support hours do not cover stands invoiced on the plan's billing history." Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after"; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible state, a charge standing invoiced on the plan's billing history, not an action or a performer; (3) it names no tool, no policy id and no snake_case or hex token; (4) its strength is exactly the edge's - "every hour ... does not cover" is the same scope as the condition, neither wider nor narrower. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only charge_controls_support_overage_c0d5009e raises a charge for uncovered support hours, the payment tool only reduces the balance and the reinstatement tool only raises a reinstatement charge. Derivation: the sentence says the settlement waits on a charge for uncovered support hours standing on the billing history; the records show fifteen history rows of which none is such a charge and the plan's support hours remaining stand at -30.5; the support overage policy's own rule says what it produces, an invoiced support overage on the plan; therefore the one action that fits is raising that overage. Handling-time condition: the plan's billing history carries an invoiced charge for the hours beyond the included pool. Resolving action: charge_controls_support_overage_c0d5009e, owner agent.
Edge B: controls_ext_reinstatement_charge waits on controls_ext_arrears_settlement. kind state_gate; gate controls_plans.balance_due; form state. Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from the reinstatement's own rule: "Remote access and alarm monitoring are restored and the reinstatement charge raised only once the balance owed under the plan stands at nil or below." Four-point test: (1) "only once" is the ordering connective; (2) the side it waits on is the balance owed under the plan, a field the plan record and the plan lookup both show; (3) no tool, id or code token appears; (4) "at nil or below" is exactly the condition, neither "reduced" nor "settled in full". Exactly one write of this difficulty takes the balance owed to nil or below: only record_controls_plan_payment_09134fd7 reduces it, the other two tools raise it. Derivation: the sentence says the charge waits on a balance at nil or below; the record shows 3130.00; the settlement policy's own rule says what it produces, the sum the owner pays to settle the plan in one payment; therefore the one action that fits is the owner making that payment. Handling-time condition: the balance owed is nil or below at the moment the plan is put back into service. Resolving action: record_controls_plan_payment_09134fd7, owner user - the caller's own act, handed over by the agent at its place in the order.
Topological order: support overage, then settlement, then reinstatement. Parallel edges: none; the tree is a chain, so there is nothing to prove commutative and no second ordering exists. Per-edge deletion sensitivity, from the Step 5 run: skipping the overage moves the settlement from 7907.81 to 4501.61; skipping the payment leaves the balance owed at 7084.72 after the reinstatement charge instead of -823.09 and drops the payment row from the terminal state. At least one problem of the tree is the customer's own write: the settlement, owner user.
The tool layer blocks nothing: see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
Write 1, subject controls_invoice_charged. Governing base policies: controls_billing_and_late_fee (no structured eligibility for this subject, so policy_scope: it fixes that extra services are invoiced on the plan in the month they are performed) and controls_portfolio_interaction, whose gate energy_subscription_point_sharing applies to controls_invoice_charged. That gate is an authorization gate with authority system_record and timing pre_action; its correlation key is energy_subscriptions.site_id and its action binding is site_id. The evidence is the owner's Energy Analytics Subscription row, standing active at the same building with data_source controls_system, which is why the point licence is carried on the automation plan and the subscription is not charged per point for the same points. No time gate applies to this write.
Write 2, subject controls_payment_received. Governing base policy: controls_billing_and_late_fee alone, with no structured eligibility for that subject, so policy_scope. No approval, status or time gate stands in front of a payment.
Write 3, subject controls_plan_reinstated. Governing base policy: controls_suspension_and_reinstatement. Of its two gates, arrears_beyond_suspension_period applies to controls_plan_suspended and therefore not to this write; restart_inside_window applies to controls_plan_reinstated and is inherited. Time anchor, copied verbatim: starting business event "the term end date"; authoritative source controls_plans.term_end_date; relation not_after; duration variants.restart_window_days; unit calendar_days; counting rule "counted forward in calendar days from the term end date, the end day excluded and the final day included"; boundary inclusive. Positive case: the term ends 2027-01-31 and the tier's window is 45 days, so the last day a restart needs no fresh survey is 2027-03-17; at 2026-09-17 the term has not even ended and the condition holds with room to spare. Negative case: at 2027-03-18, one day past the boundary, the condition fails and the system would have to be surveyed again before any plan could be quoted. The gate bites only on a plan that lapsed at its term end; this plan stands suspended for arrears and is being restored inside its own term, which is the other transition the same event covers.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The narrowest object is the single automation service plan at the Northgate Medical Office Building, plan row e7f2358d-29c3-46b6-931d-a9ccf2cb5aa4, and every aggregate in all three computations is scoped to that plan id by the runtime. Rows included: the plan year's support hours credit (16.0), the seven resolved tickets of the twelve months to the handling day, the five charge lines and the one payment. Rows excluded: nothing on this plan is excluded, because the owner holds one plan, one building, one maintenance agreement and one energy subscription - the correlation is exact rather than argued. The maintenance agreement and the energy subscription are read only, never written, and are correlated to the same site_id as the plan. Existing settlements: the 3610.00 payment of 2026-02-26 is linked to invoice INV-20260041 and settles exactly its three lines (1950.00 + 1180.00 + 480.00), so the charges standing unsettled are the two lines of INV-20260488; no reversal, compensation or adjustment exists on this plan. The support overage the agent raises carries the plan and the site as its correlation keys and lands as its own charge line on its own new invoice number.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS, AND WHAT CHANGES IF IT GOES.
The support hours credit (16.0) is the denominator of the volume-rate ladder and the pool the drawdown-order factor divides; delete it and the volume rate falls back to the tier's 156, the drawdown has nothing to draw and the overage becomes a different number.
The two on-site tickets (16.00 and 14.00 hours) put the on-site side above the visit allowance plus the pool, which is the only reason any on-site hours are billable at all and therefore the only reason the on-site rate factor bites; drop either and billable_onsite falls to zero.
The three remote tickets (6.00, 4.50, 2.50) carry the remote rate factor and, through the graphics edit among them, the re-synchronisation-time ladder of the reinstatement.
The two no-fault-found tickets are the near-miss of this task: a careless reader counts their 3.5 hours into the billable remote hours, and the rule explicitly excludes them because the tier includes a remote fix attempt and there are two of them. Delete one and the share moves from none to half, changing the answer.
The two monitoring-desk tickets carry the out-of-hours uplift; the other five reached the desk by phone, email or portal and carry none, which is the second near-miss - uplifting all 46.5 hours instead of the 8.0 that came through the monitoring desk gives a badly wrong figure.
The five charge lines and the single payment are the whole of the settlement's ledger: the count of five drives the charges-required-now ladder and the re-synchronisation clock anchor, the 2026-02-26 payment date is what makes "no payment received in the last four months" true by four days rather than by months, and the 2026-05-31 due day is both the late-fee clock and the anchor the reinstatement's method factor selects.
The suspension date 2026-07-15 is exactly 45 days after that due day, the tier's suspension period, so the world is internally consistent and the 64-day span it gives sits above the sixty-day and thirty-day thresholds of two reinstatement factors and above the 45-day restart window of a third.
The maintenance agreement (Full Coverage Agreement, active) is load-bearing four times over: drawdown order, on-site rate, on-site visit allowance and settlement discount. The energy subscription (Energy Analytics Subscription, active, twelve meters, data_source controls_system) is load-bearing twice: the shared licence allowance and the reading back-fill charge, and it is also the authoritative evidence of the base energy_subscription_point_sharing gate.
AUTOMATIC-CLAUSE CHECK. Base clauses that could fire on their own: the late fee accrues on an invoice unpaid past its due day (carried inside this task, as the settlement's late-fee factor); suspension after 45 days past due (already applied, and the seed records it); the renewal window opening 60 days before term end (2027-01-31 less 60 days is 2026-12-02, after the handling day, so it does not fire); the restart window (not reached); the alarm allowance and support pool forfeiting at plan year end (2027-01-31, not reached). Nothing ignites an obligation this task does not carry. CACHE CHECK: no stale cache is designed into this task. support_hours_remaining (-30.5), alarm_responses_remaining (48) and balance_due (3130.00) are each exactly the sum of their account's deltas in the ledger, so the displayed figures and the history agree and the difficulty comes from the policy rather than from a discrepancy.

FACTOR CARD. See computations[].factor_trace for the per-factor evidence, tier taken, value or method selected and the figure the standard method would have given, and computations[].factor_sensitivity for the recomputed baseline result of each. In summary: the support overage declares six factors of which one is a method (which hours the included pool is drawn against first) and five select values; three of them decide their tier from the building's maintenance agreement in another difficulty's product, and every one of the six is multi-source, each tier beyond the fall-through combining two conditions over distinct evidence. The settlement declares six, one method (which charges are required now) and five parameters, with the shared licence allowance decided from the owner's energy subscription and the settlement discount from the maintenance agreement. The reinstatement declares six, one method (the anchor the re-synchronisation clock starts from) and five parameters, with the gateway share decided from the maintenance agreement and the back-fill charge from the energy subscription. No base boundary was weakened: every extended policy declares overwrite [] and inherits its base lineage whole, and every new factor is built out of tier parameters the charter already publishes (support hour rate, controls technician rate, on-site visits included, gateway fee, reinstatement fee, survey fee, point overage fee, licence true-up frequency, late fee rate, billing frequency) or out of the other products' own published parameters (the maintenance tier's labor rate, repair labor discount, repair labor cover and remote monitoring; the energy tier's per-meter fee). The policy-level constants each policy adds are registered in its own params and stated in its rule in words.

PERSONA DESIGN. Dana Whitfield is written as a brisk facilities manager who says the thing she wants first and the courtesies afterwards, and the text is organised the way she would actually talk: the problem and the deadline, then what she will read off the invoice if asked, then the boundary between what the desk may do and what she will do herself, then how she reacts to what she is told. Volunteered at the opening: the company name, the callback number, the building, the symptom (the engineer could not get in and the graphics pages are dead) and the deadline. Given only when asked: the account number, the tax identification digits, the building's street, how she wants to pay, and the honest non-answers - she does not know the plan reference, she cannot date the last successful connection beyond "early summer", and she has no way of checking whether a figure is right. Passive reactions, each bound to an utterance the agent must produce first: she authorises the desk to book what has to be booked only if asked; she offers to clear what is owed only if the agent tells her something must be paid; she runs the payment herself only after the agent has handed it to her, and by ACH; she closes only after being told the plan is back on. The natural trap is that she will take the agent's word for any figure, so a wrong number is never corrected. No template labels, no numbered branches, no X-then-Y script.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. Turn by turn: she gives the company name and callback number, so find_customers resolves the account; she reads the account number and the tax digits, so verify_customer_identity passes on two matching details against a threshold of two; find_sites gives the building reference the overage charge needs; find_controls_plans gives the plan reference, the tier, the withdrawal day, the term dates, the covered points and the balance; find_controls_events gives the whole ledger the three computations reconcile; find_maintenance_agreements and find_energy_subscriptions give the two cross-product rows three of the eighteen factors turn on. Every question a real agent would have to ask has an answer in the persona, including the ones that never enter gold. Nothing waits on a real-world event: the overage is an invoice line raised on the spot, the payment is made in the conversation by the caller through the tool the agent hands her, and the reinstatement is a status change plus a charge. All of it happens under one frozen_time of 2026-09-17 10:20:00 CDT.

THE EASY MISTAKES, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM. Billing all 46.5 logged hours instead of the 2.0 on-site and 13.0 remote hours that survive the visit allowance and the pool drawdown. Billing the 3.5 no-fault-found hours, which the rule sets aside because the tier includes a remote fix attempt and there are two such tickets. Uplifting every hour for out-of-hours work instead of the 8.0 that reached the desk through the monitoring desk. Using the tier's 162 controls technician rate for the on-site hours instead of the maintenance agreement's 122. Drawing the pool proportionally, which is the standard method and gives 2296.99. In the settlement, taking only the charges already fallen due (4501.61) instead of every charge standing unsettled, or forgetting the advance instalment, the point overage or the four per cent settlement discount. In the reinstatement, counting the days from the withdrawal day rather than from the due day of the most recent plan fee charge, which is the method the tier selects and the difference between three whole months and two. Each of these is decided in prose by a sentence of the governing rule rather than by judgement.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify; read the site, the plan, the plan's whole history, the maintenance agreement and the energy subscription. Work out the support overage: hours by closure method, the visit allowance, the drawdown order, the two rates, the no-fault share and the out-of-hours uplift, giving 2462.32; raise it on the plan, the tool itself periodising the line to the calendar month it is raised in. Work out the settlement on the world that now includes it: charges required now 5592.32, late fee 251.65, advance instalment 1950.00, point overage 653.33, allowance 210.00, settlement discount four per cent, giving 7907.81; unlock the payment and hand it to the caller, who puts it through by ACH. Work out the reinstatement on the world that now includes the payment: base fee 490.00, gateway share 240.00, three whole months of re-synchronisation at 81.00, back-fill 194.40 and survey share 325.00, giving 1492.40; put the plan back into service with that charge.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The three computations were evaluated with the gate's own evaluator (skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py build_env / eval_compute / substitute) over initial_state plus the gold writes preceding each step, and the same run produced every per-factor baseline. Output: support overage result=2462.32, factor baselines 2296.99 / 2584.0 / 2542.32 / 2975.56 / 2950.32 / 2150.32, all-factors baseline 3581.64, branches 9, history rows touched 8. Settlement result=7907.81, factor baselines 4501.61 / 7666.22 / 6035.81 / 7280.61 / 8109.41 / 8237.3, all-factors baseline 3130.0, branches 12, history rows touched 7. Reinstatement result=1492.4, factor baselines 1352.4 / 1372.4 / 1411.4 / 1249.4 / 1298.0 / 1167.4, all-factors baseline 470.0, branches 5, history rows touched 6. Every factor moves the result, every all-factors baseline differs from gold, and the three figures are exactly the gold arguments at steps 8, 10 and 12. The prerequisite sensitivity run gave: skipping step 8 moves the settlement to 4501.61; skipping step 10 leaves the balance owed above nil at the reinstatement.

TWO-WAY EQUIVALENCE, FORWARD AND BACK. Forward: every binding that reads the world, aggregates, chooses or rounds carries a verbatim quotation of the rule sentence that legislates it, listed in each policy's compute_basis. Back: reading each rule through, every sentence carrying a quantity, window, filter, branch, base, order or rounding semantic is claimed by a binding - the twelve-month window by the within_months arguments, the closure-method separation by the resolution_method filters, the monitoring-desk origin by the channel filter, the drawdown order by pool_applied_to_onsite, the acting bases and the order of operations by the explicit sentence that each band of hours is priced at its own rate and the uplift added to the sum rather than applied to it, the settlement's ordering by the sentence that the allowance is taken off before the discount and the discount acts once on what is left, and the single final rounding by RND on result in all three. No sentence is left unimplemented and no filter is left unstated.

POLICY - GT CLOSURE. controls_ext_support_overage_charge -> charge_controls_support_overage_c0d5009e -> computations[0] step 8 arg charge_amount_usd -> the charge line and the raised balance. controls_ext_arrears_settlement -> record_controls_plan_payment_09134fd7 -> computations[1] step 10 arg payment_amount_usd -> the payment row and the balance at nil or below. controls_ext_reinstatement_charge -> reinstate_controls_plan_58d0efe4 -> computations[2] step 12 arg reinstatement_charge_usd -> status active, the reinstatement date and the reinstatement charge. charter_scope.extended_policies equals the set of computation policy ids, required_documents repeats it in order, and charter_scope.task_tools lists the three tools in first-call order. No fourth write hangs outside the tree and no policy of this task is left unfired.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier masked, and working only from the prose the three policies will be published as, the tool schemas, what the caller actually says and what the share lookups return: the plan stands suspended, so the request is a reinstatement; the reinstatement paragraph says the charge is raised only once the balance owed stands at nil or below, and the lookup shows 3130.00, so something must be paid first; the settlement paragraph says the sum required is fixed only after every hour of uncovered support work stands invoiced, and the history shows none, so the overage must be raised first. Working the overage paragraph over the ledger by hand gives 2462.32; the settlement paragraph over the ledger with that charge added gives 7907.81; the reinstatement paragraph gives 1492.40. The draft agrees with gold in the object, the order, the write sequence and all three figures, and it finds no second reading: the only place two readings could arise, which hours the pool is drawn against first, is settled exclusively by the maintenance agreement's standing, and the only date ambiguity, where the re-synchronisation clock starts, is settled exclusively by the tier's help desk hours and the count of charges.

REVISIONS (round 1). No defect had been found when the task was first written; the world was laid out from the factor card rather than patched to fit it, and the only adjustment made during authoring was to the on-site hours (raised so that the visit allowance plus the pool does not absorb them entirely, which would have made the on-site rate factor decorative) and to the invoice set (the office stopped raising plan fee instalments after the withdrawal, so the most recent plan fee charge is the unpaid 2026-Q2 one and the late-fee clock reads three whole months rather than nought). Both changes were propagated to the seed, the computations, the tracing and this dossier in the same pass, and the verification run above is the post-change run.


AUDIT ROUND 2 — ITEMS CLOSED AND ROUTED (audits/policy_task/controls_support_desk/_difficulty.md and 0.md).
F1 (undeclared override of base controls_support_handling and of the billing clause on extra services): closed inside the charter. controls_ext_support_overage_charge now lists controls_support_handling in base_policy_refs and declares two overwrite entries — the base sentence "The hours logged against a resolved ticket are drawn from the plan year's support pool, and once the pool is exhausted further hours are billed at the tier's support hour rate, with on-site hours billed at the controls technician rate instead." is superseded by the rule's own sentence that the hours beyond the included pool, after the visit allowance, are billed as this rule works them out at the rates the plan's records select; and the base sentence "Extra services — support hours beyond the pool, … — are invoiced in the month they are performed rather than held to the year end." is superseded by the rule's sentence that the overage is raised as one charge at the handling day covering the twelve months to it and periodised to the calendar month in which it is raised. Base's own numbers (support hour rate, controls technician rate) remain the defaults of the baseline document; only the two handling clauses are retired. The three figures the auditor derived under base (4842.00 / 4758.00) are no longer defensible readings because the clause they rest on is declared replaced.
F2 (undeclared override of the base late-fee clause): closed. controls_ext_arrears_settlement declares an overwrite of "an invoice unpaid past its due day carries the tier's late fee for each month or part month it stays unpaid", replaced by the rule's sentence that within the sum required the late fee is worked out on the charges required now for the whole months between the due day of the plan's most recent plan fee charge and the handling day, at the rate the billing frequency and those months select, and never per invoice or for a part month. The base per-invoice, part-month figure (187.80) is thereby retired for this write.
F3 (undeclared override of "the tier's reinstatement fee is charged"): closed. controls_ext_reinstatement_charge declares an overwrite of "Access and monitoring are restored when the arrears are settled in full and the tier's reinstatement fee is charged", replaced by the rule's sentence that the charge raised is the reinstatement charge this rule works out, starting from the tier's fee and adding the re-commissioning elements the records select. The base restart-window gate is not quoted and stays in force (it is still declared and satisfied in solvability_contract).
F5 (drawdown tier sentences said "only … are billed" while the compute bills both residues): closed by rewording the two tier sentences, the ladder texts and the compute_basis quotations to "…and whatever of the included hours then remains is drawn against the remote hours" / "…against the on-site hours left after the visit allowance"; the general sentence that both residues are billed now has no rival. Compute unchanged; the figure is unchanged at the value the compute always gave.
SOURCE-TASK RED (billing_period of the support overage not uniquely entailed): closed by removing the parameter from the agent's hands. charge_controls_support_overage_c0d5009e (and the two other period-bearing tools) no longer take billing_period; each stamps the line with the calendar month in which it is raised (the tool's own format contract, stated in its docstring), and the support overage rule now says so in prose ("periodised to the calendar month in which it is raised"). There is no longer a label for a solver to choose, so no second terminal hash exists. evaluation_criteria action 8 and its tracing were updated in the same pass.
T0-F8 (a wrong intermediate in computations[1].factor_trace): corrected to "6740.00 less the 3610.00 paid, that is 3130.00"; the sensitivity figure 4501.61 was and is right.
T0-O1 (maintenance agreement still active with its 90-day renewal window already open): the seed row's term now runs 2026-03-01 to 2027-02-28, so the Full Coverage Agreement's window opens 2026-11-30, after the handling day; status active and an empty renewal notice date are now consistent with the maintenance lifecycle. No factor tier moves (every maintenance ladder here reads "standing active").
Observations judged and recorded: O-2 (pool credit summed without a window) — left as is: the credit rows carry no date field the window primitives can read, the rule's words ("the support hours the plan has been credited under its entitlement") match the compute exactly, and this SEED-FRESH world carries one plan year's credit. O-3 (the one-hour guard in the proportional draw) — closed by stating it in the rule and the baseline paragraph ("the two of them together being taken as one hour where they fall below it"). O-4 ("charges raised" vs a count by due day) — closed by rewording every such sentence to "charges that fell due on the plan", which is what the count reads. O-5 (the late-fee tiers asserted "stood unpaid" without testing it) — closed by rewording the tiers to the span between the due day of the most recent plan fee charge and the handling day, which is exactly what the compute measures; the sum required is itself the unsettled balance, so the unpaid condition is carried by the quantity the rate acts on. O-6 (energy reads owner-scoped) — left: the rule says "an energy monitoring subscription the owner holds", the compute reads the owner's subscription, and this owner holds one, at this building. O-7 (the overage line carries no due day) — left: the tier's payment term is policy the agent must not have the tool apply, and the settlement rule's tier taken here requires every unsettled charge whether or not fallen due; recorded as a known limit of the row the tool writes. O-8 (the payment names no invoice) — left: the settlement is one payment across every open invoice, so the base sentence on naming an invoice is not exercised. O-9 (a credit also lowers the balance) — left: the credit rule fixes its amount from alarm rows, never from the balance, and this world has no alarm rows; the hop still resolves in one reading. O-10 — background only, nothing to do. O-11 (quarterly true-up tier differs from base "remainder of the plan year") — left unexercised; noted that a future world on a quarterly true-up tier would need an overwrite declaration on controls_agg_portfolio_point_pricing. O-12 (survey share applies the restart window to a suspended plan) — left: the extended rule takes a share of the survey fee where a lapsed plan would need a survey; it does not require a survey, so it does not conflict with the base sentence on expired plans. O-13 (credits and charges move the balance at once) — timing only; left. O-15 (the no-fault waiver grows with the count) — left as the published treatment it is.
The verification of this task was re-run after every change above with the gate evaluator: the three results, the eighteen per-factor baselines and the three all-factor baselines are exactly the figures recorded in computations, unchanged from round 1, because no change touched a value the world selects; only the prose faces, the override declarations and the tools' period stamping changed.
user_scenario:
Dana Whitfield runs facilities for Meridian Property Group, LLC out of a cramped office on the
second floor of one of their buildings, and she rings the controls desk the way she rings anyone: briskly,
with the thing she needs said first and the pleasantries afterwards. This morning the thing she needs is
simple. Her building engineer at the Northgate Medical Office Building went to load the holiday changeover
schedule into the automation system yesterday evening and could not get in at all, and the graphics pages
that normally come up on the office workstation are dead. She wants the building automation service plan at

argument_uniqueness_tracing.charge_amount_usd: 2462.32. The hours logged against resolved tickets in the twelve months to 2026-09-17 are 46.5 in all: 30.0 closed on site (16.00 on CT-401188 and 14.00 on CT-402014), 13.0 closed remotely (6.00 on CT-401360, 4.50 on CT-401622, 2.50 on CT-402310) and 3.5 closed with no fault found (2.00 on CT-401790 and 1.50 on CT-401955); the included support hours standing to the plan's credit are 16.0. The building carries a maintenance agreement standing active whose tier does not include remote monitoring of covered equipment, so the plan year absorbs one on-site attendance beyond the tier's two, that is three attendances at four hours, 12.0 hours, leaving 18.0 on-site hours. The tier includes on-site escalation and the maintenance agreement stands active, so the 16.0 included hours are drawn first against those 18.0 on-site hours, leaving 2.0 on-site hours billable and all 13.0 remote hours billable. The 46.5 hours logged are at least twice and less than three times the 16.0 credited and two tickets were closed on site, so the remote hours carry the tier's support hour rate of 156 less six per cent, 146.64. The maintenance tier carries a repair labor discount of twenty per cent, so the on-site hours carry that agreement's own regular-hours labor rate of 122 rather than the tier's 162. The tier includes a remote fix attempt and two tickets were closed with no fault found, so none of those 3.5 hours is billed. The tier's help desk answers extended hours and two resolved tickets reached the desk through the monitoring desk carrying 8.0 hours, so an uplift of a quarter of 156, that is 39.00, is charged for each of those hours. 13.0 x 146.64 + 2.0 x 122 + 0 + 8.0 x 39.00 = 1906.32 + 244.00 + 312.00, giving 2462.32 rounded once to two decimal places.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain, not a fan-out: the settlement has exactly one prerequisite and the reinstatement has exactly one, so no two writes may be freely reordered and there is nothing to prove commutative. The order is forced twice over. Skipping ahead to the settlement before the overage is invoiced gives 4501.61 instead of 7907.81 because the charges standing unsettled are 3130.00 rather than 5592.32, and skipping ahead to the reinstatement before the payment lands leaves the balance owed at 5592.32, which is not nil or below.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the support overage charge and replaying everything else leaves the charges standing unsettled at 3130.00 instead of 5592.32, so the settlement the owner pays falls from 7907.81 to 4501.61 and the terminal balance owed under the plan changes with it.

Skipping the owner's payment leaves the terminal state without the 7907.81 payment row and with the balance owed at 7084.72 rather than -823.09 after the reinstatement charge, and the plan would have been put back into service while the balance still stood above nil, which is the standing the reinstatement charge waits on.
